text:
maya: incident-bot just fired an SLO burn alert for /generate: burn_rate=4.9x over 5m and 1.8x over 1h. paging criteria hit. Anyone on primary?
incident-bot: ALERT: service=/generate SLO_BURN high. windows: 5m=4.9, 30m=2.1, 1h=1.8. Pager duty: paged oncall.
sam: I'm on. seeing a spike in 5m tokens served + a flurry of 500s from a partner tenant. digging into traces.
jordan: looking at metrics — tail latency spiked around 12:42 UTC, but 1h window is still below page threshold previously. this looks like a short-lived flash.
lee: customer-impact check: any customer-facing errors? alert says increased error budget burn but downstream retries might be inflating counts.
maya: prelim: ~3% of requests for a single partner are returning 5xx, but error % across all tenants is ~0.6. That partner has bursty traffic pushing longer sequences.
alex: ok that matches: heavy long-context requests -> more KV misses -> higher latency -> service timeouts for their client. Not system-wide.
emily: can we reduce paging noise by changing multi-window policy? current rule pages if 5m burn > 4x OR 1h burn > 2x. That made this page even though 1h is still low.
sam: +1 to revisiting. For immediate mitigation, I've throttled that partner's api key at the edge to reduce tail.
ops-bot: ACTION: throttle applied to partner-id=acct-772, rate-limit=50r/s.
jordan: after throttle, 5m burn dropped to 1.6x. Good.
maya: thanks. For postmortem/tuning: proposal to add a "flooring" condition so pages only fire when both a short window AND a longer window exceed smaller thresholds, e.g., page if (5m>3x AND 30m>1.5x) OR (1h>2.5x). This aims to avoid transient flashes paging oncall.
lee: alternative: require sustained burst for two consecutive 5m windows before paging. That would be easy to implement in alerting rules.
emily: either approach could reduce noise. we should be careful not to hide true incidents where rapid collapse matters. Maybe mark low-severity transient pages as slack-only (no phone page) unless also matches long-window condition.
sam: agreed. Operationally, change could be: keep 5m for slack alerts, require 30m or 1h for paging.
alex: also worth adding an absolute floor on raw error count. right now percent-based rules can trigger on tiny baselines. "error_count > 50 AND burn_rate> X" would prevent tiny-tenant churn from paging.
jordan: good call. Example alert rule patch (Datadog / PromQL pseudocode):
```
ALERT slo_burn_high_paging
IF (burn_rate_5m > 3 AND burn_rate_30m > 1.5 AND sum_errors_5m > 50) OR (burn_rate_1h > 2.5 AND sum_errors_1h > 100)
FOR 5m
LABELS {severity="page"}
```
maya: let's capture that in a follow-up change. Also need a new dashboard tile showing multi-window burn overlays and per-tenant absolute error count so oncall can quickly triage.
emily: I'll spin up a dashboard draft: tiles -> SLO burn (5m/30m/1h), per-tenant 5m error count, top 10 tenants by token length distribution.
lee: runbook change: add step to check top-tenant list and apply temporary throttle/unblock policy. Also add step: 'if >3 tenants crossing thresholds -> escalate to infra'.
sam: for immediate post-incident changes I'll update the paging rule to slack-only for 5m-only triggers and include the sum_errors floor. Will post the PR link here.
ops-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/alerts/1234 (slo_burn: add error_count floor + change 5m->slack-only).
jordan: nice. Can we also run a backtest on 30/60 day history to estimate how many pages we'd have suppressed? need to ensure we don't regress coverage.
emily: I'll run a backtest against stored burn metrics and post results by EOD.
maya: owners: emily (dashboard/backtest), sam (alert rule PR + deployment), lee (runbook update), jordan (post-change monitoring windows), alex (partner contact & followup).
alex: I'll reach out to partner about sequence length patterns and ask for pacing. cc: acct-owner.
maya: one more thought: we should add a small cooldown per tenant so they can't oscillate the page repeatedly (eg: per-tenant page cooldown 30m).
jordan: agreed. that solves flappy tenants.
emily: notes for metrics team: add a derived metric `slo_burn_per_tenant` if possible. current aggregates hide spikes.
sam: after PR merges, I'll monitor burn and slack alerts for 24h and report. If suppressions look safe, we'll promote rule changes to paging policy.
maya: thanks everyone. good mitigation work. let's keep the thread for the followups. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: RESOLVED: paging alert closed at 12:55 UTC after throttle and rule change mitigation.
ops-bot: REMINDER: owner assignments saved in https://confluence.internal/incident-playbooks/slo-burn-tuning
alex: filed a customer follow-up ticket: TKT-9001.
emily: backtest initial results: the proposed rule reduced hypothetical pages by ~62% with <1% loss in detection for incidents that had >5 tenants impacted. I'll attach detailed graphs in the PR.
maya: perfect. we'll aim to merge tomorrow morning after review.
lee: small todo: add examples to runbook showing how to flip 5m slack-only flag in the alert manager UI.
sam: noted. tagging rotation for oncall: @maya will be primary for the rollout window.
maya: OK, thanks. closing planning for now.
__meta: Generated Slack thread representing an SLO burn alert, mitigation, and follow-up tuning discussion. Contains root message + replies in chronological order.
